evidence.summary: books table: id integer primary key, title text not null, author text (nullable).
GET /api/books returns every book as a JSON array of {id, title, author}; no paging, no filter, no auth.
ratings table: book_id integer references books(id), stars integer with check (stars between 1 and 5); no primary key, no uniqueness.

PUT /api/books/{id}/rating reads JSON field 'stars', rejects values outside 1-5 with 400 {"error": "stars must be 1 to 5"}, otherwise inserts a new ratings row (appends; never updates) and returns {"ok": true}.

GET /api/books/export returns JSON (code comment: 'JSON, not CSV'): one {title, stars} object per book-rating pair from a left join, so unrated books have stars null and a book rated twice appears twice.
Storage is SQLite through Python's sqlite3, file named by SHELFIE_DB (default shelfie.db), one module-level connection.
SHELFIE_SESSION_SECRET is read at import (startup fails with KeyError without it); nothing else in the file uses it. Value not recorded.
One process: the standard library http.server HTTPServer on port 8080 with a single Handler class.
No handler checks identity or a session; no DB.commit() call anywhere; unmatched GET/PUT paths send no response; there is no endpoint to add, edit or delete a book.
README claims: export the library as CSV at GET /api/v1/books/export.csv.
README claims: rate books from 1 to 10.
README claims: data is stored in PostgreSQL.
README claims three services (catalog, ratings, gateway), pointing to docs/architecture.md.
Architecture doc claims three services behind a gateway (catalog, ratings, gateway doing auth and routing), each with its own database.
OpenAPI 3.0 spec v1.0 lists GET /api/v1/books (List books).
Spec lists GET /api/v1/books/export.csv (Export the library as CSV).
Spec lists PUT /api/v1/books/{id}/rating with body field 'score', integer, minimum 1, maximum 10.

SQLite does not enforce 'references' unless PRAGMA foreign_keys is on (it is never set), so a rating for a missing book id would be accepted; and with no commit, writes are visible to the running process but would be lost when it exits. Deduced from sqlite3 defaults; the code was not run (not approved).

architecture.frontend: none: JSON over HTTP only, no UI
architecture.backend: single-process Python http.server with one Handler and one shared SQLite connection (the documented three-service gateway design does not exist in the code)

features.name: Browse the book library
features.description: List every book in the library with its title and author.
features.observed_behaviour: GET /api/books returns a JSON array of {id, title, author} for all rows of books, unpaged and unfiltered, with no authentication.
features.business_logic: title is required (not null); author is optional. There is no endpoint to add, edit or delete books, so how books enter the library is not in the code.
features.integration: Needs a way to add books in the unified app (none exists in Shelfie); needs per-user ownership if several people use it.

features.name: Rate a book (1-5 stars)
features.description: Give a book a whole-number rating from 1 to 5 stars.
features.observed_behaviour: PUT /api/books/{id}/rating with JSON {"stars": n}; n outside 1-5 gives 400 {"error": "stars must be 1 to 5"}; otherwise a new ratings row is inserted and {"ok": true} returned. Rating again adds another row instead of replacing the first.
features.business_logic: stars is an integer 1..5, enforced in the handler and by a CHECK constraint. Ratings are appended, never updated; there is no user on a rating. The README and OpenAPI spec say 1-10 with field 'score'; the code (which wins) says 1-5 with field 'stars'.
features.integration: Needs the unified Book; should become one rating per user per book (PUT replaces) in the unified app.

features.name: Export library with ratings (JSON)
features.description: Download the library as JSON: each book's title with its star rating.
features.observed_behaviour: GET /api/books/export returns a JSON array of {title, stars} from books left-joined to ratings: unrated books have stars null; a book rated several times appears once per rating.
features.business_logic: Output format is JSON, not CSV, despite the README and spec. Only title and stars are exported (no id, no author).
features.integration: Needs the unified Book and Rating; duplicate rows per multiple ratings should not carry over once ratings are one per user per book.

contradictions.summary: README promises CSV export at GET /api/v1/books/export.csv; the code serves JSON at GET /api/books/export
contradictions.resolution: the code wins: JSON export of {title, stars}; CSV is listed in unknowns as an unbuilt claim

contradictions.summary: OpenAPI lists GET /api/v1/books/export.csv (CSV); the code has GET /api/books/export (JSON)
README says ratings are 1 to 10; the handler and the CHECK constraint allow 1 to 5
OpenAPI says PUT /api/v1/books/{id}/rating with field 'score' 1-10; the code takes 'stars' 1-5 at /api/books/{id}/rating
contradictions.resolution: the code wins: field 'stars', 1-5, path without /v1

contradictions.summary: OpenAPI lists GET /api/v1/books; the code serves GET /api/books
README says PostgreSQL; the code uses SQLite via sqlite3
README says three services (catalog, ratings, gateway); the code is one process
contradictions.resolution: the code wins: a single-process app

contradictions.summary: docs/architecture.md says a gateway does auth and each service has its own database; the code has no auth and one database
contradictions.resolution: the code wins: no auth, one SQLite database; SHELFIE_SESSION_SECRET is an unused leftover

unknowns: CSV export: claimed by README and openapi.yaml, contradicted by the code (JSON only). Treated as a claim, not a feature. Would be settled by the user saying CSV is wanted in the new app.
1-10 rating scale and the 'score' field: claimed by README and spec, contradicted by the code (1-5 'stars'). Settled as 1-5 per 'trust what the apps actually do'.
PostgreSQL storage and the three-service gateway architecture with per-service databases: claimed by README and docs/architecture.md, not present in the code.
The /api/v1 version prefix: claimed by the spec only.
Purpose of SHELFIE_SESSION_SECRET: required at startup, never used; would be settled by the user.
How books get into the library: there is no create, edit or delete endpoint; perhaps inserted into the database by hand. Would be settled by the user.
Whether writes persist: the code never commits, so ratings would be lost when the process exits (inferred from sqlite3 defaults; the code was not run because running source code was not approved).
Whether appending several ratings per book is intended (a rating history) or a bug: the export repeats books rated more than once.
